statements: Colleagues want to hand files around through a browser. Add GET /files/<name>, which sends the named file from the shared folder (the shared/ directory of the service).
Folders inside the shared folder work the same way, to any depth: GET /files/<folder>/<name> sends a file that is in a folder.

GET /files/ shows a web page that lists what is in the shared folder, and GET /files/<folder>/ does the same for a folder. Each entry shows its name and, for a file, its size in bytes. The name is a link that opens the file or the folder.
The link of every entry opens that entry, whatever it is called.
In every listing the entries come in the order the README describes for file lists.

A file arrives exactly as it is stored, whatever its kind or size, with the content type that fits it (for example text, JSON, CSV, PNG, PDF; a kind we do not know is sent as a generic binary file). Text follows the README's rule for text.

Large files can be fetched in parts, so that an interrupted download can continue: a client that asks for a range of bytes gets just those bytes, and a range that does not exist in the file is refused in the standard way.
Anything that does not exist gives the usual not-found answer, and a method other than GET on these addresses gets the usual wrong-method answer.
Everything that exists today keeps working exactly as it does now.
The README documents the new addresses.
The new behaviour has tests in test/. Keep the change focused on what this ticket needs.
brief: Add the file download and folder listing addresses under /files/ to the share service as the numbered ticket statements describe, document them in the README and add tests under test/. Follow the conventions already in the code. Change only what the ticket needs.
